title: Ram Sahay v. Rajasthan Government
text: The petitioner-workman, Ram Sahay, served as a daily wage worker with the Public Works Department for 14 years. His services were terminated without notice or retrenchment compensation under the Industrial Disputes Act. The workman raised an industrial dispute. The Labour Court found that the workman had attained the status of a 'workman' under the Industrial Disputes Act by virtue of continuous engagement exceeding 240 days per year for more than 5 consecutive years. Termination without following Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act is void ab initio. The employer was directed to reinstate the workman with back wages. This writ petition by the State challenging the award is dismissed. The Industrial Disputes Act protects workmen against arbitrary retrenchment. The reinstatement order and 75% back wages are upheld.
